Definition: Self-giving, sacrificial love that seeks the highest good of the other — the love God is, shows in Christ, and pours into His people.
BiblicalUsage: Agape was a fairly ordinary Greek word until the New Testament filled it with cross-shaped meaning. God 'is agape,' demonstrated it while we were still sinners, and commands it as the mark of His people.
TheologicalSignificance: Agape is love that acts, gives and stays. Because God loved us first at such cost, our love for others can be patient, kind and unafraid.
